body: This adds an error that wasn't there before, and in opening a random real project in the editor, I get this error printed out like 50 times. I'm really not sure what it's coming from - I don't see anything in the project's code, and I don't really see anything in Godot calling it either... :-/

I wonder if it might be coming from the editor generating docs? And perhaps it's happening for this project because it uses a GDExtension, and the docs are being generated too early? Those are just some random guesses, though

Once again I'm too eager to consistently handle invalid state 😅
I think it's out of scope to try and fix this for now, so I just reverted to the "silently fail" implementation with a comment.

I think we need to have a different process to mark a `GDType` as `FINALIZED` during the registration ("type loading") component, rather than lazily when a subclass is registered.

Otherwise this leaves any GDType without a subclass in a perpetual non-finalized state

`p_no_inheritance` might be better replaced with a two-value enum. While I can understand what `p_no_inheritance` means, it reads really weird. If this wasn't already in use by the existing code, I don't think I would consider this _at all_.

I think I would either change it to (a) an enum, `LookupMode.SELF_ONLY` / `LookupMode.SELF_AND_SUPER` (alternatively `LookupMode.ALL` since it's shorter), or (b) invert the condition, so that it becomes `p_self_only = true`.

The enum reads better out of context. `get_enum_map(LookupMode.SELF_ONLY)` is going to be understandable regardless of knowing this method declaration
These seem duplicated
What is this doing? It looks slightly like magic

Do we need to place this as an inner class? If we continue along this path we're going to end up with a giant hunk of inner class declarations here, which IMO really muddles trying to understand what the class itself is about.

This is another thing which is really pervasive across the codebase which might be better avoided in new code. However... Are we doing this because we're not using namespaces anywhere? Why are we not using namespaces?

This is a fairly complicated method. It has side effects and restrictions on the inputs. As we do this migration, this is one example of a method that _definitely_ needs a strong doc comment.

I don't feel qualified to write it and I don't really understand the internal representation of enums here enough to even put together a draft.

Prefer explicit `!= nullptr` over implicit conversion to bool for readability
```suggestion
		if (_enum_info != nullptr) {
```

Use `const_cast` when switching between qualifications over C-style casts. Unless we have a secret coding guideline on this that I don't know about :p 
```suggestion
			EnumInfo *enum_info = const_cast<EnumInfo *>(*_enum_info);
```
Should we add forwarding methods to whatever `t` is here (looks like `ClassInfo`?) so we don't need to do `t->gdtype->thing` and can directly invoke `t->thing`?
Worth filing a bug report for and linking the ticket here. A simple `TODO` will get lost for eternity
Same thing here as the comment on the `TODO` above. It's pretty concerning this is getting invoked in an invalid state so often.

Agreed. A good contender is right at the end of the registration call.
However, this is also somewhat risky regarding non complying objects and might need additional integration to make it work. That's why I've pushed it off for this PR and want to approach it in a follow up.

We currently don't do this much in the codebase.
The reason is likely because C++ does not offer a lot of support for using enums. In languages like Swift, using them is extremely convenient, but in C++, you may have to look up the enum and write it out, which makes is cumbersome and verbose. 

I do agree that `get_enum_map(true)` is perfectly obtuse as to its behavior. I did consider making it an enum, but in this case, the enum would have to be placed in `GDType` because of namespacing. The lookup would actually be `get_enum_map(GDType.LookupMode.SELF_ONLY)` (or `get_enum_map(GDType.SELF_ONLY)`), which is very verbose (and in the latter requires non `enum struct`).
It is, it's taken directly from the `ClassDB` implementation. I do not like it either but we need to be backwards compatible.

We aren't strictly _not_ using namespaces, but it hasn't been a priority either.

I do agree that inner classes aren't great for a few reasons. Namespaces could be one solution, or perhaps we make it `GDEnumInfo` or something. On the other hand, it isn't a problem right now, with it being small and not needing to forward declare it, so maybe we should ignore it for the moment and change it if it does become a problem.
Documenting these functions is (imo) out of scope for the PR, especially because they're not called directly (instead through the macro).
We do use c-style casts in the codebase a lot more than the specialized casts, and yea it's a bad practice.
I don't think `t->gdtype->thing` is bad at all, it exposes that it's just doing a `gdtype` forward.
Agreed, will do on merge

It is definitely magic. I wonder if we could try removing it and see what happens...? It simply shows up in this [9-year old commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/36e0a72c77348d4a1f2195937dff8dba88f7e044) with basically no explanation.

I'm struggling to think of what it's supposed to be doing anyway. It looks like it's trying to do something which converts `OuterClass.Enum` to `Enum` but that feels _really_ wrong to be doing right here. Plus it would fail on `Outer.Inner.Enum` as that would give you `Inner`.
For our own sanity we'd be better to start now. If we start placing things here we're going to hit an inertia wall to ever changing it.

It's out of scope for this PR to change behavior, especially for an exposed method.
If you want to remove it, I suggest a follow-up PR.
I wonder if it has a similar root cause as to why the splitting on `.` is being done in `bind_integer_constant`...
Yeah not the end of the world, just wanted to see thoughts on it
`t` is `ClassDB::ClassInfo` which is not exposed, so it doesn't have convenients methods at all.
My IDE auto-inserts the space when I commentify the code. Do we really need to remove the space?
Yes we do this to improve code readability, which IMO does help a lot, see [here](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/code_style.html#comment-style-guide)
